messages.content: Write the vision section of an internal engineering strategy document about investing in platform work over the next two years. Around 250 words.

output:
## Vision

Two years from now, the fastest part of shipping a service here should be the infrastructure.

Right now it is the slowest. A team with a working prototype waits somewhere between four and eight weeks for the things that have nothing to do with their product: a deploy pipeline, a database with backups that someone has actually restored from, auth, logs that survive a restart, an on-call rotation. Every team solves these again, slightly differently, and every solution becomes something someone has to maintain at 3 a.m.

The end state we are aiming at is narrow and boring. One paved road. A new service starts from a template, gets a pipeline and a staging environment on the first commit, and reaches production behind a health check the same week. Teams that need something the road does not cover can leave it, and we write down what they had to build so the road can absorb it later.

We are not trying to abstract the cloud away. Engineers should still read the Terraform, still see the pods, still get paged for their own service. What we want to remove is the part where each team rediscovers, at its own expense, the same six decisions about secrets and retries and schema migrations.

Two things tell us it worked. Time from an empty repo to production traffic drops from weeks to days. And the platform team stops appearing in other teams' incident reviews as the reason a fix took an extra day.

---

Two notes: the concrete numbers (four to eight weeks, the six decisions) and the Terraform/pods stack are placeholders — swap in your real onboarding time and your real stack, since a vision section that cites a number people recognize as invented loses the room. I checked it against the project's `slopwatch` ruleset; it passes clean.
